title: MyVector — real-dataset benchmark
subtitle: MySQL 8.4 / 9.7 / 26.10 + MariaDB 12.3 · fashion-mnist-784 · published ground truth
description: MyVector's native HNSW vector search on a real ann-benchmarks dataset (fashion-mnist-784-euclidean: 60,000 × 784-d image embeddings, L2), scored against the dataset's published exact ground truth — the ann-benchmarks recall methodology, not a brute-force self-check. Queries come from the dataset's held-out test set (never indexed). Same engines and hardware as the synthetic dashboard; this one answers "what recall/throughput do you actually get on real embeddings?"
caveats:
⚡ Kernel optimization in review (PR #278): MyVector's HNSW distance kernel was running scalar on every build/arch (hnswlib's SIMD is x86-only and gated off; GCC won't auto-vectorize the float reduction at -O3). Vectorizing it to NEON/SSE (a scoped reassociation pragma, pgvector's flags) gives, in a same-session A/B on this host/dataset (two freshly-built 8.4 components, median of scalar n=3 / SIMD n=6 clean runs, identical recall):
metricscalarSIMDΔ
index build83.8 s45.6 s1.84× faster
QPS @ recall 0.997 (ef=50)487553+14%
QPS @ recall 0.999 (ef=200)352434+23%
QPS @ recall 1.000 (ef=800)203278+37%
All three · PR #278 (NEON) series (brighter colors) plot the measured optimized builds on the same A1 host/slice — a direct before/after against each scalar version. Optimized medians: 8.4 82.5s→46.4s build, ef=200 352→434 QPS; 9.7 82→46s, 355→438; 26.10 82→45s, 354→444 — all recall@10 0.999. The muted scalar series are the pre-optimization builds still in main (until PR #278 merges). The gain grows with ef_search (more distance evals per query); it does not fully close the gap vs pgvector at low ef, which is per-query execution overhead, tracked separately.
Dataset: fashion-mnist-784-euclidean (ann-benchmarks) — 60,000 train × 784-d, 10,000 held-out test queries, L2/Euclidean. Index HNSW M=16, ef_construction=200.

Recall@10 vs published ground truth: each query is scored against the dataset's published exact top-10 neighbors, so recall is directly comparable to ann-benchmarks numbers — not the brute-force self-check the synthetic dashboard uses.

ef_search sweep 10→800 is measured warm (a discarded warmup pass runs first). The headline ANN QPS / latency / recall@10 cards and table are taken from the warm ef_search=200 sweep point, so every engine is compared at the same operating point. MyVector loads its whole index into memory at build; MariaDB warms its mhnsw graph cache lazily over the first ~1k queries, so a cold first-query measurement would understate it.
Exact KNN is the brute-force baseline (full scan, ~0.3 QPS at 60k×784) — it exists to show how much the HNSW index buys you, not as a practical option.

MariaDB cache: mhnsw_max_cache_size raised to 1 GiB (its 16 MB default thrashes to disk). MariaDB builds HNSW online during insert, so its "index build" is load time (no separate build phase) — much slower here (~240 s) but, once warm, its search is competitive-to-faster than MyVector on this dataset at recall ≈ 1.0.

MariaDB ef_search floor: MariaDB floors mhnsw_ef_search to ~2×M (≈32), so an ef_search=10 request is not a valid operating point for it — that point is omitted from MariaDB's plotted curve (its measured value is kept in the result JSON under ef_search_excluded). Every other engine applies no such floor, so their ef_search=10 points are plotted as-is. MariaDB's remaining curve (ef≈20→800) is monotonic once each point is warmed per-ef; the headline uses the warm ef=200 point.
Hardware: all engines on the same Ampere A1 host, each pinned to an identical 4 vCPU / 24 GB slice. 26.10 is the current MySQL Innovation release.
